comp_011:n1.prompt:
You are helping me set up the recurring board meeting cadence using {{vendor}}, our scheduling tool. Goal: create a durable, conflict-free recurring board slot so minutes stay on a predictable schedule.

First, ask me for anything missing: (1) the cadence frequency (e.g., monthly, quarterly) and preferred day/time window, (2) meeting duration, (3) timezone, (4) the list of board members and their email addresses, (5) which calendars (Google, Outlook, Apple) should be connected to {{vendor}} for conflict checking, and (6) any standing out-of-office or blackout periods to respect.

Once I provide these, using my configured credentials for {{vendor}}:
- Define or update an availability schedule reflecting our working hours and any date overrides/out-of-office periods.
- Create the recurring board meeting as an event or booking on that schedule, set to repeat at the cadence I specified, with all board member emails invited.
- Confirm that all connected calendars are checked for conflicts before finalizing the recurring booking.
- If {{vendor}} exposes an MCP server or tool-calling surface, use it end-to-end (check availability, book, and confirm) rather than requiring me to use the dashboard.

Done looks like: a recurring board meeting series exists in {{vendor}}, invitations are sent to all board members, the cadence and duration match what I specified, and no calendar conflicts remain unresolved.

Report back with: the event/schedule name created, the recurring cadence and next three upcoming dates, the list of invited board members, and any conflicts or scheduling issues you found and how you resolved them (or flag them for me if they need my decision).

comp_011:n2.prompt:
You are helping me prepare a reusable board meeting minutes template in {{vendor}}, our project-management tool, as part of keeping our board minutes on cadence.

If you don't already have this information, ask me for: (1) my {{vendor}} workspace/organization details and confirmation you can access it with my configured credentials, (2) the standard board meeting agenda items we use (e.g., call to order, approval of prior minutes, financial update, officer/committee reports, old business, new business, executive session, adjournment), (3) the names/titles of standing attendees (directors, officers, counsel) to pre-list, and (4) where in {{vendor}} our board records should live (a specific project, folder, or space).

Actions to take:
1. In {{vendor}}, use its template feature to start a new document from a pre-built or blank template suited for meeting minutes.
2. Build out the minutes template with sections for: meeting date/time/location, attendees present and absent, quorum confirmation, approval of prior minutes, each standing agenda item I provided, action items with owners, and space for signature/date at the end.
3. Organize this template alongside our other project docs and notes in {{vendor}}, in the folder/space I specified, so it's easy to find each cadence cycle.
4. Name the template clearly (e.g., "Board Meeting Minutes Template") and confirm it can be duplicated for each new meeting without altering the master copy.

Done looks like: a saved, reusable minutes template exists in {{vendor}} in the correct location, containing all standard sections and pre-listed attendees, ready to be duplicated before each board meeting.

Report back with: the location/link of the template within {{vendor}}, a summary of the sections included, and any gaps (e.g., missing agenda items or attendee names) you need me to fill in before it's finalized.

comp_011:n3.prompt:
You are helping me prepare for an upcoming board meeting so the minutes-taking process runs smoothly, even though holding the meeting itself remains a human step. Please do the following:

1. Ask me for: the meeting date/time, the video conferencing tool I'll use (e.g., Zoom, Google Meet), the list of directors and any invitees expected to attend, and the agenda items or resolutions to be discussed.
2. Using my existing minutes template (ask me to share the file or its current draft if not already available), pre-fill the header fields: company name, meeting date, meeting type (regular/special), location or dial-in method, and the expected attendee list marked as 'present' or 'absent' placeholders for me to update live.
3. Draft a structured skeleton inside the template with sections for: call to order/quorum confirmation, approval of prior minutes, each agenda item with space for discussion summary and motion/vote/resolution language, and adjournment.
4. Prepare a short checklist for whoever takes notes during the meeting (e.g., capture motions verbatim, record votes by name, note abstentions/recusals, timestamp key decisions).
5. Set a calendar reminder or note for me confirming the meeting is scheduled, so the live session isn't missed.

Done looks like: a ready-to-use minutes template with pre-filled logistics, a clear agenda-mapped skeleton for real-time note capture, and a note-taker checklist — all ready before the meeting starts. Since directors must actually convene, deliberate, and have someone capture what is decided in real time, this remains a human step and I will conduct and record the live meeting myself.

Report back with: the finalized template content (or a summary if the file is long), the checklist, and confirmation of what's ready versus what still needs my input before the meeting.

comp_011:n4.prompt:
You are helping me circulate our approved board meeting minutes for signature using {{vendor}}, our legal-ops e-signature platform. Ask me for any missing inputs: the finalized minutes document (or its location in our data room/drive), the list of board members/signers with names and emails, the required signing order (if any), and our standard reminder/expiration policy (e.g., remind every 3 days, expire after 14 days).

Once you have these, do the following in {{vendor}} using our configured credentials:
1. Upload or link the finalized minutes document.
2. Add all required signers with correct emails, and set the signing order if sequential approval is required (e.g., chair signs first).
3. Configure automatic reminders and an expiration date per our policy.
4. Set any signature fields, dates, and titles needed so each signer's block is clearly marked.
5. Prepare a short cover message to signers noting the meeting date and that this is the official corporate record copy.

Do NOT send the signature request. Because a human must explicitly approve before this goes out, assemble everything as a ready-to-send draft: signer list with order, reminder/expiration settings, and the cover note, and present them to me for review.

When the draft is ready, report back: the document name/version, the full signer list with roles and signing order, the reminder/expiration schedule, and a link or reference to the pending request in {{vendor}}. Then stop for human sign-off — I will review and manually trigger the send once I approve. Do not submit, send, or finalize the routing yourself.

comp_011:n5.prompt:
You are helping me file our latest signed board minutes into our {{vendor}} data room and keep the corporate record properly organized. If you don't already know, ask me for: (1) the location of the fully signed minutes file, (2) the folder path or location in {{vendor}} where board minutes/data room documents live (or ask me to confirm the correct parent folder if unsure), and (3) any naming convention or metadata fields I want applied (e.g. meeting date, quarter, minute number, resolution tags).

Once you have these, using my configured credentials for {{vendor}}:
1. Locate the target data room folder for board minutes (search by path/name if needed).
2. Upload the signed minutes file into that folder via the API, using a clear filename that includes the meeting date.
3. Set custom metadata/properties on the file (e.g. meeting date, minute number, status=signed, resolution tags) so it's queryable later.
4. Confirm the file's version history is intact (list revisions) so future updates remain auditable.
5. Review and set appropriate access permissions — ensure board members/relevant parties have view or download access consistent with our existing data room access pattern, without over-broadening permissions beyond what's already in place for similar documents.

Done looks like: the signed minutes file is uploaded into the correct data room folder, tagged with the right metadata, permissions match our standard data room access pattern, and the file is retrievable/listed correctly via the API.

Report back with: the final file location/path, the metadata values you set, a summary of who has access, and confirmation that upload and permissioning succeeded. If any permission change affects new parties outside our normal access list, flag that explicitly and stop for human sign-off before finalizing those grants.
